claim: Alignment from models to enforcement. Engineering models express obligations that the environment can enforce through constraints on actions or states, and through evidence evaluated at gates. Sensors obtain evidence from artifacts and executions, including through static and dynamic analysis. Gates can also require results from constraint checks. These functions may be combined in one mechanism; each governs only the obligations and evidence within its scope.
topology: New chapter-opening overview; obligations feed direct constraints and evaluation rules, sensors supply evidence, and gates control admission. No internal caption, title, or legend.

redesign: New chapter-opening overview; obligations feed direct constraints and evaluation rules, sensors supply evidence, and gates control admission. No internal caption, title, or legend.
alt: Engineering models supply selected obligations. One branch restricts agentic work through constraints; another supplies evaluation rules derived from modeled obligations. Sensors obtain evidence from the work. Gates use evidence, evaluation rules, and optional constraint-check results to admit work or refuse it for revision. Constraints can also enforce directly without a gate.
